narrative_purpose: Show that the Medusoid's mechanism already exists on Earth at tiny scale: a Portuguese man o' war float beside the vast bell, the same crested gas sac five hundred times apart.
subject: A scale comparison in one frame. On the LEFT, drawn large and detailed as a specimen study, a Portuguese man o' war: a small iridescent gas-filled float with a raised crest along its top and long thin tentacles trailing beneath it, with a tiny human silhouette beside it for scale showing it is only about a hand's length. On the RIGHT, the same crested gas-float shape repeated at enormous size as the Medusoid's dome, with a tiny human silhouette at its base now almost invisibly small against it.
scene: Both specimens presented against a plain deep indigo study background, the left one as if just lifted from water with faint wet highlights, the right one as if seen high in air with faint haze.
camera: Flat comparative specimen framing, both subjects seen from the same side angle so the shared crested-float form reads clearly.
light: Cool even specimen lighting; iridescent cyan and faint magenta sheen on the small float, pale translucent glow on the great dome.
palette: Iridescent cyan and a touch of magenta on the man o' war, pale translucent cyan on the dome, deep indigo surround.
detail_level: Crisp on both float forms and their crests; backgrounds plain and empty.
composition: Small specimen on the left third, giant on the right two thirds, both aligned on a common baseline, plain dark space above both for later callout labels.
consistency_notes: The shared FORM is the whole point: both must read as the same crested gas-float solution at wildly different sizes. Human silhouettes convey scale without any numbers or scale bars. Dome matches fig-00-cover.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no scale bars, no rulers, no 3D-render or photographic look, no cartoon style
